html:
SMTO-BOOT-0004 — This part of SMTO isn't installed on this computer

GUID: ee5c8509-e305-4b08-aadd-3c230e9c60c3
Slug: boot-environment-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The command looked for SMTO's installed program files (the .venv folder) next to it and didn't find them, so it stopped. Usually the installer hasn't been run here yet, or the folder was moved or deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run the installer that matches what you're starting: ./install.sh for SMTO, ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh for a Linux Gateway, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on a Mac, or src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Each part keeps its own program files, and only its own installer creates them.
  2. Run the original command again from the same project folder. The command only looks in its own folder, so a copy installed somewhere else isn't found.
  3. If you moved or copied the project folder, run the installer again in the new location instead of copying the old .venv folder across. The installed program files remember where they were created, so a moved copy can't be used as it is.

What success looks like

  • The command starts normally and no longer reports missing program files.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal message, including the Error reference line, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or the Gateway's pairing to start fresh; reinstalling doesn't need that.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A startup, reset, reset-pairing or setup script could not find its product virtual environment (a .venv directory with an executable python) at the expected path beside the script.

What this means

  • Startup/setup/reset checks cannot find the expected virtual-environment directory or executable at the selected product path. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Startup/setup/reset checks cannot find the expected virtual-environment directory or executable at the selected product path.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the checkout, platform-specific environment path and executable before creating a replacement elsewhere.

How to fix it

  • Run the matching installer to create the environment: install.sh for the root .venv used by startup.sh and setupplaywright.sh; src/gateway_agent/install.sh or src/gateway_macos/install.sh for the Gateway .venv used by startup.sh, reset.sh and reset-pairing.sh; src/gateway_windows/install.ps1 for .venv\Scripts\python.exe used by reset.ps1. Preserve AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR and Gateway pairing state, and do not copy a .venv between paths.
  • Run the matching platform installer for this controller or Gateway, then start it again. Preserve existing state databases.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching installer supplies the expected environment and the intended launcher resolves it.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
